themes_detail.label: Animal Intrusions in Parks Surge
themes_detail.summary: Animal complaints in Bed-Stuy parks spiked to 18 THIS WEEK, a 586% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 2.6 weekly complaints (z-score: 7.07), suggesting a new or spreading wildlife problem requiring immediate investigation into cause and scope.
evidence: 18 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.07 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Community board has recurring requests for park maintenance and expansion, suggesting underlying park condition issues
reporting_angles: What species are residents encountering and where in the district's parks?
Interview DPR about recent animal activity and whether it's tied to park maintenance backlogs or food waste issues

themes_detail.label: Maintenance Crisis at City Facilities
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints more than tripled THIS WEEK to 25 complaints, a 218% spike above the 8-week baseline of 7.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 2.89), indicating potential failures across public buildings or infrastructure systems.
evidence: 25 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 2.89 indicates significant statistical deviation
Community board repeatedly requests enhanced health/safety inspections and facility upgrades
reporting_angles: Which city agencies and facilities are generating the complaints—schools, recreation centers, DPR facilities?
Is this tied to deferred maintenance from budget constraints or recent staffing cuts?

themes_detail.label: Encampment & Homelessness Crisis Escalates
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 12 LAST WEEK (638% above 8-week baseline of 1.6) while homeless person assistance requests also spiked to 12 LAST WEEK (317% above baseline of 2.9), suggesting a rapid deterioration in conditions affecting public spaces and a persistent gap in services the community board has requested for years.
evidence: 12 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.9)
12 homeless person assistance complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.37)
Community board has standing, recurring budget requests for homeless services, indicating this is a chronic, unmet need
reporting_angles: Where are encampments appearing and what triggered the sudden spike last week?
Interview DHS, outreach teams, and community residents about capacity limits and service gaps in Bed-Stuy

themes_detail.label: Public Sanitation & Hygiene Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Public urination complaints exploded to 4 THREE WEEKS AGO with a 3100% spike above the 8-week baseline of 0.1 complaints per week (z-score: 11.72), while food poisoning complaints reached 4 TWO WEEKS AGO (540% above baseline of 0.6), together signaling potential sanitation and public health hazards that may be linked to encampment growth.
evidence: 4 urination-in-public complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.72, highest severity)
4 food poisoning complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.97)
Community board requests increased health and safety inspections for restaurants and facilities
reporting_angles: Are food poisoning clusters linked to specific vendors or restaurants? Request DOHMH inspection data.
Is public urination tied to encampment locations and lack of public restroom access, or a separate issue?

themes_detail.label: Paradoxical Parking Enforcement Decline
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints dropped 45% to 88 TWO WEEKS AGO, falling sharply below the 8-week baseline of 160.9 weekly complaints (z-score: -2.8), which may signal reduced enforcement activity, a data reporting lag, or shifting neighborhood dynamics worth understanding.
evidence: 88 illegal parking complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 160.9 weekly average (45% decline)
Z-score of -2.8 indicates statistically significant drop
Contrasts with sustained high volume (1,934 complaints over 90 days) suggesting temporary fluctuation
reporting_angles: Has NYPD parking enforcement staffing or activity changed recently in Bed-Stuy?
Is this a data collection artifact or genuine shift in parking violations?
